title: drive budgets count raw processed tokens, so caps measure context re-reads, not cost
detail: usage.Usage.tokens = input+output+cache_write+cache_read, each weighted 1, and drive.budget_tokens / drive.session_budget_tokens compare that total. Measured on pinned-engine: 17.1M total = cache_read 16.53M (96.5%), cache_write 0.49M, output 0.11M, input 348. Weighted by price (cache read 0.1x, 1h cache write 2x, output ~5x input) that is ~3.2M input-equivalent, yet drive stopped budget_exceeded at 16.6M vs the 8M cap. Model price differences (opus vs haiku) are ignored too. A budget should compare a cost-weighted measure from one declared price table; keep raw tokens visible as telemetry.

resolution.verify: uv run python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_cost_budget.py
